outcome: Respiratory function monitor (RFM) measurements (tidal volumes, rates of airway obstruction, mask leak)
cohort: 70 preterm infants requiring resuscitation at birth, participating in the Sustained Aeration of Infant Lungs (SAIL) trial.
finding: Expiratory tidal volumes of both sustained inflations and IPPV were highly variable, and vital signs were similar between groups throughout resuscitation, indicating sustained inflation was not superior to IPPV for promoting lung aeration in this study subgroup.
followup_time: Observations taken during resuscitation at birth.
